codex_consult.feedback_summary: Codex confirmed 3-AC granularity is right; AC3 must stay separate from AC2 (parsing alone is insufficient — propagation is the user's explicit ask); argument-hint frontmatter is in scope as metadata for the new flag (count under --codex edit, not as a separate feature). Three concrete plan bugs flagged: (1) AC1 must cover BOTH initial Section 5 population (Step 3) AND multi-turn appends (Step 4) — single-placement near L49 leaves Step 4 uncovered; (2) AC3 must cover the spec-subagent re-dispatch inside the split-QA retry loop (Step 6 sub-step 3 retry block at lines 175-205), not only the initial dispatch — otherwise --codex silently drops on QA fail/retry; (3) parse order matters — strip --codex BEFORE the empty/non-empty branch decision in Step 1 so `/spec --codex` (no requirement) correctly enters clarification ask while preserving codex_required=true. Codex also confirmed low meta-violation risk if prohibition stays plain prose without nested example trees, and reaffirmed scope hold (no agents/spec.md edit, no validators).
codex_consult.feedback_incorporated: All three concrete bugs incorporated into the spec: (1) M1 wording explicitly requires the prohibition be 'positioned so it visibly governs both Step 3 first-write and Step 4 multi-turn append' and AC1 mirrors this; (2) M3 wording explicitly enumerates 'spec-subagent dispatch (sub-step 2), QA validation dispatch (sub-step 3), AND the split-QA retry re-dispatch path (sub-step 3 retry block at lines 175-205)' and AC3 mirrors this with 'covers all three dispatch sites — initial spec-subagent, initial QA, retry-loop re-spec-subagent'; (3) AC2 explicitly requires the strip happen 'BEFORE the empty/non-empty branch decision (current lines 18-19)' with edge case documented in Edge Cases & Risks. Granularity and frontmatter scoping accepted as drafted.
